newsitem.title: USA: Crown says Texas union claims dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Crown says Texas union claims dismissed.

text.p: Crown Central Petroleum Corp on Tuesday said a federal mediator dismissed claims that a union lock-out at its Pasadena, Texas refinery violated federal labor laws.

The independent refiner and marketer said the decision by a general counsel of the U.S. National Labor Relations Board clears the way for renewed talks on a new labor pact with the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Worker's Union.

"We are hopeful that other outstanding issues between the company and (union) can now be resolved by further negotiations and that this will lead to a new contract at the Pasadena facility," said Henry Rosenberg, Crown chairman and chief executive officer.
Crown on February 5 locked out workers at the 100,000 barrel per day refinery near Houston after some equipment at the plant was vandalized as talks stalled on a new labor pact with the union.
The union has since filed several additional unfair labor practice claims and called for a boycott of Crown stations.
Negotiators with the OCAW Local 4-227 and Crown are slated to meet again on Wednesday to consider a union proposal to settle the 11-month lock-out.
